article_content: Razvan Dumitru, a Big Issue seller from Romania, stole £50 from Jane Phillips, a blind 66-year-old pensioner, as she attempted to give him money. Despite the Big Issue's requirement that sellers be homeless or facing financial hardship, Dumitru resides in a four-bedroom terraced house in Edmonton, North London, valued at £250,000. Dumitru snatched five £10 notes from Phillips's purse when she tried to give him £1 for food. Shoppers nearby detained the 22-year-old until police arrived. Phillips stated that Dumitru had previously stolen from her, but she had forgiven him, believing he was homeless. However, it has since been revealed that Dumitru and his family have lived on a desirable street in Edmonton for approximately two years. In November 2011, the house was advertised for rent at £1,600 per month, described as 'immaculate' with three double rooms, one en suite, two bathrooms, a good-size garden, a large reception area, and a newly fitted kitchen. Neighbors confirmed Dumitru's residency, despite Big Issue rules. Dumitru's mother laughed when questioned about her son's crime and acknowledged he was awaiting sentencing. His father responded with 'So?' when contacted. A local shopkeeper reported banning the family from his store and noted that luxury cars frequently visited the property at night. He mentioned that it was unclear how many people lived in the house but that they appeared to have money, driving BMW and Mercedes vehicles. The incident raises questions about Dumitru's eligibility to sell The Big Issue, a job meant for homeless individuals, especially considering his prior convictions. At the time of the theft from Phillips, Dumitru was serving a suspended prison sentence for stealing an iPhone in December 2011 at Caffé Nero in Clapham Junction, South London. He had also been banned from the Morrisons in Sutton, where the recent theft occurred, for shoplifting. Morrisons security guard Lisbona Addo confirmed Dumitru was known for shoplifting and had previously been arrested by him. Dumitru admitted to the crime against Phillips before Croydon magistrates and is currently in custody awaiting sentencing. Phillips believes Dumitru should be deported, stating that criminals from other countries should not be allowed to remain in the UK. A Big Issue spokesman stated that Dumitru had been selling 'on and off' for several months but was not a consistent vendor. The charity relies on referrals from councils regarding vendors' homelessness status, but acknowledges this system is 'far from reliable'. Last year, it was revealed that one in three Big Issue vendors (700 out of 2,250 nationwide) were from Romania. A loophole in EU immigration rules allows Big Issue sellers to claim 'self-employed status' and receive benefits. The Big Issue stated that new vendors undergo an induction process and sign a code of conduct, the breach of which results in disqualification from selling. John Bird, the founder of The Big Issue, has stated that it is about decriminalizing the homeless. In a separate incident, Emil Metodiev, a Bulgarian citizen with multiple theft convictions in Bulgaria, was jailed for burglary just nine days after arriving in Britain. He was caught stealing valuables from a home in Southend, Essex. The lifting of restrictions on Romanian and Bulgarian citizens on January 1 has raised concerns about a potential influx of individuals who may struggle to find work and end up homeless or selling The Big Issue. British politicians have clashed with Romanian Minister for Labour Mariana Campeanu, who stated that her country's citizens take jobs shunned by British workers and that the UK should be 'grateful' for the extra labor. She also stated that only a tiny minority of people will come to Britain hoping to claim benefits or commit crimes. Other politicians have raised concerns about monitoring immigrants with criminal histories and preventing those with few means from becoming homeless.

Il padre di Dumitru ha semplicemente risposto: 'E allora?' quando è stato contattato. Il negoziante ha detto che non era chiaro quante persone vivessero nella casa, ma sembrava che avessero soldi, guidando BMW e Mercedes. L'incidente solleva dubbi sull'idoneità di Dumitru a vendere The Big Issue, un lavoro destinato ai senzatetto, soprattutto considerando i suoi precedenti penali. Al momento del furto a Phillips, Dumitru stava scontando una pena sospesa per aver rubato un iPhone nel dicembre 2011 al Caffè Nero di Clapham Junction, a sud di Londra. Era stato anche bandito dal supermercato Morrisons di Sutton, dove è avvenuto il recente furto, per taccheggio. La guardia giurata di Morrisons, Lisbona Addo, ha confermato che Dumitru era conosciuto nella zona per taccheggio e lo aveva già arrestato. Dumitru ha ammesso il reato contro Phillips davanti ai magistrati di Croydon ed è attualmente in custodia cautelare in attesa della sentenza. Phillips crede che Dumitru debba essere espulso, affermando che ai criminali provenienti da altri paesi non dovrebbe essere permesso di rimanere nel Regno Unito. Un portavoce di Big Issue ha detto che Dumitru aveva venduto 'a intermittenza' per diversi mesi, ma non era un venditore regolare. L'organizzazione si affida alle segnalazioni dei comuni sullo stato di senzatetto dei venditori, ma riconosce che questo sistema è 'tutt'altro che affidabile'. L'anno scorso, è stato rivelato che un venditore di Big Issue su tre (700 su 2.250 a livello nazionale) era rumeno. Un cavillo nelle norme UE sull'immigrazione consente ai venditori di Big Issue di richiedere lo 'stato di lavoratore autonomo' e ricevere sussidi. The Big Issue ha dichiarato che i nuovi venditori seguono un processo di inserimento e firmano un codice di condotta, la cui violazione comporta la squalifica dalla vendita. John Bird, il fondatore di The Big Issue, ha detto che si tratta di depenalizzare i senzatetto. In un episodio separato, Emil Metodiev, un cittadino bulgaro con precedenti condanne per furto in Bulgaria, è stato incarcerato per furto con scasso solo nove giorni dopo essere arrivato in Gran Bretagna. È stato sorpreso a rubare oggetti di valore da una casa a Southend, nell'Essex. L'abolizione delle restrizioni ai cittadini rumeni e bulgari il 1° gennaio ha sollevato preoccupazioni circa un potenziale afflusso di persone che potrebbero avere difficoltà a trovare lavoro e finire per diventare senzatetto o vendere The Big Issue. I politici britannici si sono scontrati con il Ministro del Lavoro rumeno, Mariana Campeanu, la quale ha affermato che i cittadini del suo paese accettano lavori che i lavoratori britannici non vogliono e che il Regno Unito dovrebbe essere 'grato' per la manodopera extra. Ha anche affermato che solo una piccola minoranza di persone verrà in Gran Bretagna sperando di richiedere sussidi o commettere crimini. Altri politici hanno sollevato preoccupazioni su come monitorare gli immigrati con precedenti penali e su come impedire a chi ha pochi mezzi di diventare senzatetto.

article_content: Chelsea will face NK Maribor at Stamford Bridge on Tuesday, marking their first encounter with the Slovenian team. After a 1-1 draw against Schalke in their previous home game, the Blues need a win to secure a smooth progression to the Champions League knockout stage. Who exactly are these visitors from Slovenia? Let's delve into their background. First, a brief history. Maribor has recently dominated Slovenian football and is aiming for a fifth consecutive title. The club was established in 1960 following the dissolution of NK Branik, another Maribor club that was disbanded after being accused of poisoning opponents before a playoff match. Maribor survived a bribery scandal in the early 1980s, leading to their relegation to the Yugoslav third division. Following Slovenia's independence, they won the first Slovenian Cup in 1992. Since then, they have accumulated twelve league titles and seven more cups. This season marks their second appearance in the Champions League group stage. How is Maribor performing this season? Luka Zahovic, the son of Slovenian football icon Zlatko, has been a standout player. They are currently third in the league, six points behind the leaders Domzale, but with a game in hand and remain strong contenders for the title, despite a recent 2-1 home defeat to Celje. Their squad includes the league's top scorer, Luka Zahovic, with eight goals. Zahovic's name might sound familiar because he is the son of Zlatko Zahovic, Slovenia's all-time greatest player and record goalscorer, who now serves as the director of football at Maribor. Luka was born in Portugal during his father's time playing there and joined Benfica's youth academy before moving to Maribor as a teenager. He is a Slovenia youth international but is also eligible to play for Portugal and is fluent in Slovenian, Portuguese, English, and Spanish. Who else should we watch? Brazilian striker Marcos Tavares is a club legend. The captain has scored 121 goals in eight seasons with Maribor and became the club's all-time leading scorer in May. He is a skillful and daring player and is definitely one to keep an eye on. Who is the manager? Ante Simundza served as an assistant to Darko Milanic, the current Leeds manager, for three seasons before taking over in 2013. He was a player in 1999 when Maribor reached the Champions League group stages, finishing last in their group with four points from matches against Lazio, Dynamo Kiev, and Bayer Leverkusen. Darko Milanic, now managing Leeds, previously managed Maribor for five seasons. What can we anticipate from Maribor? Expect them to be well-organized and play compactly, likely with Tavares as a lone striker. They have secured two draws against Schalke and Sporting Lisbon and defeated Celtic to qualify for the group stages. They will aim to frustrate Chelsea, hoping that Tavares or Zahovic can score a goal. However, considering the difference in squad quality, Chelsea is expected to win comfortably.

Ma chi sono questi avversari provenienti dalla Slovenia? Scopriamo qualcosa di più sul loro conto. Innanzitutto, un po' di storia. Era un giocatore nel 1999, quando il Maribor ha raggiunto la fase a gironi della Champions League, finendo ultimo nel girone con quattro punti, frutto delle partite contro Lazio, Dinamo Kiev e Bayer Leverkusen. Darko Milanic, ora allenatore del Leeds, ha allenato il Maribor per cinque stagioni. Cosa possiamo aspettarci dal Maribor? Saranno ben organizzati e compatti, con Tavares probabilmente unica punta. Hanno ottenuto due pareggi contro Schalke e Sporting Lisbona e hanno battuto il Celtic per qualificarsi alla fase a gironi. Proveranno a mettere in difficoltà il Chelsea, sperando che Tavares o Zahovic, magari entrando dalla panchina, possano segnare un gol. article_content: By Lizzie Parry He is the man behind the popular 5:2 diet. But despite championing the phenomenon known as 'The Fast Diet', Dr. Michael Mosley decided to try another, historical method to shed pounds: tapeworms. Well-known for self-experimentation, the science journalist infected himself with a tapeworm – one of the most unpleasant parasites known to humans. Scroll down for video Parasite: Dr. Michael Mosley holds up a tapeworm during his new program. He infected himself with the tapeworm to see if he would lose weight, but he actually gained 2lbs after his appetite for carbohydrates increased. The results of his experiment will be broadcast during a new program called 'Infested! Living With Parasites,' which will air on BBC4 next month as part of the corporation's Natural History month. The documentary follows Dr. Mosley as he lives with the parasites in his gut for six weeks. Historically, tapeworms were thought to be a weight-loss aid, with Victorian women swallowing the parasites' eggs in an attempt to lose weight. But Dr. Mosley found he actually gained weight, adding 2lbs, during his stint as a human guinea pig. He also revealed that health and safety regulations meant the BBC cleared him to consume the tapeworms – which can grow to several feet in length in the intestines – but drew the line at him deliberately getting head lice, even though it affects millions of schoolchildren each year. Intestine: Dr. Mosley realized there was a tapeworm (pictured) inside him when he swallowed a camera to see whether the cysts had transformed into tapeworms. He had three parasites in his gut. Dr. Mosley said his weight gain could have been caused by the need to increase his food intake as a result of the parasites living in his gut. 'I was keeping a food diary to see if my food preferences changed,' he said. A tapeworm is a parasite that can live in a person's intestines. They tend to be flat, segmented, and ribbon-like. Humans can catch them by touching contaminated feces and then putting their hands near their mouth, swallowing contaminated food or water, or by eating raw contaminated pork, beef, or fish. Many patients do not know they have a tapeworm infection until they see segments of the worm in their stools. Symptoms include stomach pain, vomiting, diarrhea, weight loss, malnutrition, and changes in appetite. A beef tapeworm, as swallowed by Dr. Mosley, remains in the intestines and is easily treated with tablets. Other tapeworms can cause serious problems as they can settle in other parts of the body. Tapeworm infections are most common in developing countries; they are rare in the UK. Source: NHS Choices 'I think I probably ate a bit more chocolate. Tapeworms like beer and chocolate – they like carbohydrates.' 'My weight if anything went up a bit. One of the theories is that the tapeworm probably encourages you to eat more. You feed it.' In order to infect himself with the tapeworm, Dr. Mosley traveled to Kenya where his team tracked down the parasite, harvesting cysts from the tongue of an infected cow in an abattoir in Nairobi. The cysts form in infected cattle and contain baby beef tapeworms, which can live for up to 20 years. Dr. Mosley swallowed three cysts. 'It's not something you can easily lay your hands on,' he said. 'My wife's a GP and she was not very keen but she said it was OK because beef tapeworm is relatively innocuous. And also, it is not infectious.' Six weeks later, Dr. Mosley swallowed a camera to see whether the cysts had transformed into tapeworms. Linked to his iPad, the camera revealed that Dr. Mosley had three parasites growing in his gut. The beef tapeworm makes its home in the intestine and is safer than other forms of the parasite. The pork tapeworm, in contrast, is far more dangerous, moving around the body. They can cause brain cysts in humans. Scientists have been increasingly fascinated by the effects of parasites on the human body. It has become widely accepted that their eradication in most parts of the world has led to a rise in allergies and many other conditions. Historically, tapeworms were thought to help people lose weight. But Dr. Mosley's experiment revealed he gained 2lbs, the result, he suspects, of his increased appetite. 'I like finding out stuff through my personal experience of it,' Dr. Mosley said. 'They get very few people who are prepared to be infected by tapeworms. Hopefully my feces will contribute at some time in the future to a better test.' 'There was a time when Victorian ladies would swallow tapeworm eggs in the hope that it would help them lose weight, but this was actually a fallacy because the eggs are not infectious to human beings – they are only really infectious to cattle.' 'It is part of the peculiar life-cycle of the beef tapeworm that when you pass segments and eggs, they have to be eaten by a cow before they become infectious.' Producer Nathan Williams said that BBC policies allowed Mosley to consume the tapeworm because it could not be passed from human to human, but parasites such as pinworm and head lice fell foul of guidelines. However, he was allowed to experiment with the lice as long as they were placed on his arm. 'It's fine to eat a tapeworm but they wouldn't let us have a pinworm even though 40 per cent of the children in the UK have it,' Mr. Williams said. 'Similarly they wouldn't let us give head lice in the hair because you might give it to other people and it wouldn't be fair to infect Michael's family and his friends.' The tapeworms were killed off using pills, although the team had not been able to trace the bodies being expelled from Dr. Mosley's body. He said: 'Nothing came out. There are two possibilities: the most likely possibility is that the pills killed the worms and my body digested the tapeworms which is an ironic end - parasite gets eaten by its host, which is most likely.' 'The second possibility is they are still there, but since it is about 13 weeks since I swallowed the cysts, I think I would have noticed by now.'
translated_content: Di Lizzie Parry È l'uomo dietro la popolare dieta 5:2. Ma, nonostante sia un sostenitore del fenomeno noto come 'The Fast Diet', il dottor Michael Mosley ha deciso di provare un altro metodo storico per perdere peso: i vermi solitari. Ben noto per la sua auto-sperimentazione, il giornalista scientifico si è infettato con un verme solitario – uno dei parassiti più sgradevoli conosciuti dall'uomo. Scorri verso il basso per il video Parassita: il dottor Michael Mosley mostra un verme solitario durante il suo nuovo programma. Si è infettato con il verme solitario per vedere se sarebbe dimagrito, ma in realtà ha guadagnato 2 libbre (circa 900 grammi) dopo che il suo appetito per i carboidrati è aumentato. I risultati del suo esperimento saranno trasmessi durante un nuovo programma chiamato 'Infested! Living With Parasites', che andrà in onda su BBC4 il mese prossimo come parte del mese della storia naturale dell'emittente. Il documentario segue il dottor Mosley mentre convive con i parassiti nel suo intestino per sei settimane. Storicamente, si pensava che i vermi solitari aiutassero a perdere peso, e le donne vittoriane ingoiavano le uova dei parassiti nel tentativo di dimagrire. Ma il dottor Mosley ha scoperto di aver effettivamente guadagnato peso, aggiungendo 2 libbre (circa 900 grammi), durante il suo periodo come cavia umana. Ha anche rivelato che le normative sulla salute e la sicurezza hanno fatto sì che la BBC gli desse il permesso di ingerire i vermi solitari – che possono crescere fino a diversi metri di lunghezza nell'intestino – ma si sono rifiutati di lasciarlo infestare deliberatamente dai pidocchi, anche se questi colpiscono milioni di scolari ogni anno. Intestino: il dottor Mosley si è reso conto di avere un verme solitario (nella foto) dentro di sé quando ha ingoiato una telecamera per vedere se le cisti si fossero trasformate in vermi solitari. Aveva tre parassiti nel suo intestino. Il dottor Mosley ha detto che il suo aumento di peso potrebbe essere stato causato dalla necessità di aumentare l'assunzione di cibo a causa dei parassiti che vivono nel suo intestino. 'Stavo tenendo un diario alimentare per vedere se le mie preferenze alimentari cambiavano', ha detto. Un verme solitario è un parassita che può vivere nell'intestino di una persona. Tendono ad essere piatti, segmentati e simili a nastri. Gli esseri umani possono contrarli toccando feci contaminate e poi portando le mani alla bocca, ingerendo cibo o acqua contaminati, oppure mangiando carne di maiale, manzo o pesce crudi contaminati. Molti pazienti non sanno di avere un'infezione da verme solitario finché non vedono segmenti del verme nelle loro feci. I sintomi includono dolore allo stomaco, vomito, diarrea, perdita di peso, malnutrizione e cambiamenti nell'appetito. Un verme solitario bovino, come quello ingerito dal dottor Mosley, rimane nell'intestino ed è facilmente curabile con delle compresse. Altri vermi solitari possono causare problemi seri, poiché possono depositarsi in altre parti del corpo. Le infezioni da verme solitario sono più comuni nei paesi in via di sviluppo; sono rare nel Regno Unito. Fonte: NHS Choices 'Penso di aver probabilmente mangiato un po' più di cioccolato. Ai vermi solitari piacciono la birra e il cioccolato: amano i carboidrati.' 'Il mio peso, se possibile, è aumentato leggermente. Una delle teorie è che il verme solitario probabilmente ti incoraggi a mangiare di più. Lo nutri.' Per infettarsi con il verme solitario, il dottor Mosley si è recato in Kenya, dove il suo team ha rintracciato il parassita, prelevando cisti dalla lingua di una mucca infetta in un mattatoio a Nairobi. Le cisti si formano nel bestiame infetto e contengono larve di verme solitario bovino, che possono vivere fino a 20 anni. Il dottor Mosley ha ingoiato tre cisti. 'Non è qualcosa che si trovi facilmente', ha detto. 'Mia moglie è un medico di base e non era molto entusiasta, ma ha detto che andava bene perché il verme solitario bovino è relativamente innocuo. E, inoltre, non è contagioso.' Sei settimane dopo, il dottor Mosley ha ingoiato una telecamera per vedere se le cisti si fossero trasformate in vermi solitari. Collegata al suo iPad, la telecamera ha rivelato che il dottor Mosley aveva tre parassiti che crescevano nel suo intestino. Il verme solitario bovino si stabilisce nell'intestino ed è più sicuro di altre forme del parassita. Il verme solitario suino, al contrario, è molto più pericoloso, poiché si muove per il corpo. Può causare cisti cerebrali negli esseri umani. Gli scienziati sono sempre più affascinati dagli effetti dei parassiti sul corpo umano. È ormai ampiamente accettato che la loro eradicazione nella maggior parte delle parti del mondo abbia portato a un aumento delle allergie e di molte altre condizioni. Storicamente, si pensava che i vermi solitari aiutassero le persone a perdere peso. Ma l'esperimento del dottor Mosley ha rivelato che ha guadagnato 2 libbre (circa 900 grammi), e sospetta che ciò sia dovuto al suo aumentato appetito. 'Mi piace scoprire le cose attraverso la mia esperienza personale', ha detto il dottor Mosley. 'Ci sono pochissime persone disposte a farsi infettare da vermi solitari. Spero che le mie feci contribuiscano in futuro a un test migliore.' 'C'è stato un tempo in cui le signore vittoriane ingoiavano uova di verme solitario nella speranza che le aiutassero a dimagrire, ma questa era in realtà una credenza infondata, perché le uova non sono infettive per gli esseri umani: lo sono solo per il bestiame.' 'Fa parte del peculiare ciclo vitale del verme solitario bovino: quando si espellono segmenti e uova, questi devono essere ingeriti da una mucca prima di diventare infettivi.' Il produttore Nathan Williams ha detto che le politiche della BBC hanno permesso a Mosley di ingerire il verme solitario perché non poteva essere trasmesso da persona a persona, ma parassiti come gli ossiuri e i pidocchi non rientravano nelle linee guida. Tuttavia, gli è stato permesso di sperimentare con i pidocchi, a condizione che fossero posti sul suo braccio. 'Va bene mangiare un verme solitario, ma non ci permetterebbero di avere un ossiuro, anche se il 40% dei bambini nel Regno Unito ne è affetto', ha detto Williams. 'Allo stesso modo, non ci permetterebbero di mettere i pidocchi nei capelli, perché si potrebbero trasmettere ad altre persone e non sarebbe giusto infettare la famiglia e gli amici di Michael.' I vermi solitari sono stati eliminati con delle pillole, anche se il team non è stato in grado di accertare l'espulsione dei corpi dal corpo del dottor Mosley. Ha detto: 'Non è uscito niente. Ci sono due possibilità: la più probabile è che le pillole abbiano ucciso i vermi e che il mio corpo li abbia digeriti, il che è un finale ironico: il parassita viene mangiato dal suo ospite, il che è molto probabile.' article_content: A former civil servant, Dr. Angelika Hibbett, who was dismissed after claiming expenses for a meditation course, is suing the Government for £1 million. Dr. Hibbett alleges she endured 'workplace stress and bullying' from superiors while employed at the Home Office in London, which exacerbated her mental health issues. She was terminated for gross misconduct after submitting a £390 claim to cover a 'relaxation and meditation' training course intended to alleviate her depression. The Government has refuted these allegations, asserting that Dr. Hibbett, who earned £63,000 annually, was 'defensive and unwilling to accept criticism'. Joining the Home Office in 2007, Dr. Hibbett served as a programme director in the crime and policing group’s research and analysis unit. According to her statement to the tribunal, she was 'diagnosed with work stress-related anxiety and depression'. She stated that she opted for the relaxation and meditation therapy course after her doctor advised her that she would require medication for a 'long time'. The 56-year-old claims that the £390 expenses claim for the course was initially approved by automatic government software, according to The Evening Standard. However, she repaid the amount when her superiors threatened gross misconduct charges, the tribunal heard. Dr. Hibbett contends that her health deteriorated as a result, and she experienced further stress and bullying at work. Consequently, she claims she was dismissed in 2010, despite being on sick leave for over four months. Stephen Webb, the crime and policing group’s director of finance and performance, informed the tribunal that the expenses claim constituted 'insubordination' and that it was his duty to 'safeguard public money'. He stated that his department had 'bent over backwards to accommodate Angelika'. The tribunal is scheduled to conclude today.

article_content: Dan Evans' hopes for a strong US Open showing are dashed after a first-round qualifying loss at Flushing Meadows. The British No. 3, playing out of Birmingham, held a match point in the second set against Jimmy Wang but ultimately fell 4-6, 7-6 (11/9), 6-2. A year ago, Evans enjoyed a significant breakthrough in New York, qualifying and advancing to the third round. That run included a close match against Tommy Robredo, who subsequently defeated Roger Federer, a match Evans arguably should have taken to a fifth set. However, Evans has not progressed as much as he or British tennis officials would have liked, partly due to a persistent knee injury. Facing Wang, the 16th seed and world No. 132, was a difficult first-round draw. Evans fought to win the first set and showed resilience after missing an early break chance in the second. He narrowly lost the tie-break, with Wang saving Evans' match point with an ace and capitalizing on errors from the British player. Wang carried the momentum into the final set, and Evans could not recover. This defeat is expected to significantly lower Evans' ranking from its current 176, potentially into the 200s. He will need to rediscover his form from last summer to prevent further decline. In contrast, James Ward secured a comfortable victory over Aldin Setkic of Bosnia, 6-2, 6-2, and will face Vincent Millot of France in the second qualifying round. Ward, currently ranked at a career-high of 131 following a strong performance on North American hard courts, has ambitions to reach the main draw in New York for the first time. Ward was the only one of five British players to advance, with Dan Smethurst joining Evans in exiting the tournament on Wednesday. VIDEO: Murray needs to step up - McEnroe.

article_content: Harvey Nichols, the designer department store, is known for its attention-grabbing marketing strategies. Past campaigns have included a model appearing to wet herself in excitement for a seasonal sale, a 'walk of shame' television advertisement, and bulldogs carried around in expensive handbags. Their new Summer Sale campaign takes a more lighthearted approach, using humor to get noticed. The campaign, created by adam&eveDDB, uses the phrase 'run around like a headless chicken' and features headless chickens dressed in Spring/Summer 2013 collection items, with the tagline, 'The Harvey Nichols Sale. Try to stay calm'. Julia Bowe, Group Press and Marketing Director at Harvey Nichols, said the campaign captures the 'frantic effect' the sale has on customers. She added that the 'headless chicken' concept portrays this in a fun, light-hearted way and highlights the excitement of finding the perfect sale purchase, with discounts of up to 50 per cent off. Photographed by Daniel Stier, the campaign features chickens wearing an MSGM lace dress, a Zegna sport jacket, and a Valentino clutch. Ben Tollett and Emer Stamp, Executive Creative Directors at adam&eveDDB, joked that they were 'running around like headless chickens' trying to come up with the idea. In June 2012, Harvey Nichols faced criticism for an advertisement depicting a woman who appeared to wet herself with excitement. In March 2013, images promoting a Liverpool beauty hall featuring models seemingly kissing their reflections also drew complaints. The Advertising Standards Authority (ASA) received complaints about the latter campaign, citing concerns about its suitability for children and religious offensiveness. However, this new campaign signals a shift towards more fanciful and fun advertising. The Harvey Nichols Summer Sale launches online at 10am on Tuesday, June 11th, and in-store on Wednesday, June 12th, offering discounts of up to 50 per cent off.

article_content: President Barack Obama announced Tuesday he has invited Democratic and Republican leaders from both the House and Senate to a White House meeting on Thursday. The purpose is to discuss deficit reduction and the necessity of raising the federal debt ceiling. Obama stated that he wants the meeting to "build on the work that's already been done and drive toward a final agreement." This agreement would address expanding federal deficits and secure congressional approval for increasing the government's borrowing limit. Senate Minority Leader Mitch McConnell, who previously invited Obama to address Congress on the issue, will attend the White House meeting, according to his office. Senate Majority Leader Harry Reid also plans to attend. House Speaker John Boehner indicated his participation but cautioned that Congress would reject tax increases sought by Obama and the Democrats. "I'm happy to discuss these issues at the White House, but such discussions will be fruitless until the president recognizes economic and legislative reality," Boehner, R-Ohio, said in a statement. He added, "I'm pleased the president stated today that we need to address the big, long-term challenges facing our country." Obama, in an unscheduled appearance in the White House briefing room, said that deficit reduction talks with congressional leaders over the Fourth of July weekend showed progress but that "we still have to work through some real differences." Obama urged both parties to move out of their "comfort zone," emphasizing that "this should not come down to the last second." White House spokesman Jay Carney later conveyed Obama's belief that the issues involved in reaching a comprehensive agreement to reduce federal deficits by up to $4 trillion over the next decade are well-understood. Carney said it is now time for difficult decisions, with both sides compromising to reach an agreement beneficial to the entire nation. "The ideal will never become law, whether you're a conservative House Republican or a liberal Democrat or the president of the United States," Carney stated. "You're never going to get everything you want, because our system doesn't work like that." The Senate reconvened on Tuesday, cutting short its planned weeklong Fourth of July recess, with leaders resuming discussions on federal deficit negotiations amid the approaching deadline to raise the government's debt ceiling. The three-day Fourth of July weekend did little to alter the rhetoric surrounding deficit reduction talks and the need for Congress to increase the government's borrowing capacity. In his opening remarks after the Senate reconvened, Reid, D-Nevada, accused Republicans of endangering the nation's economic recovery by threatening to oppose an increase in the government's borrowing limit. McConnell, R-Kentucky, responded by accusing Democrats of seeking increased spending as a solution to the deficit problem. Prior to Obama's invitation, McConnell reiterated his call for Obama to address Congress and hear Republican concerns about any agreement involving tax increases. Reid stated his party's willingness to compromise but rejected Republican efforts to prioritize the interests of "a few millionaires and billionaires" over those of the broader population. With House members scheduled to return on Wednesday, congressional leaders remain sharply divided over the conditions to be attached to an increase in the current $14.3 trillion debt ceiling. Republicans insist on deep spending cuts and the exclusion of tax increases as preconditions for any increase. Democrats are seeking to minimize cuts to social services and advocate for the elimination of specific tax breaks and loopholes benefiting wealthier Americans. Treasury Department officials and leading economists have warned of potentially catastrophic consequences if the debt ceiling is not raised by August 2, which could lead to a default on the nation's debt obligations. Such a default could trigger skyrocketing interest rates and a collapse of the dollar, among other adverse effects. Increasing the debt ceiling would enable the government to borrow additional funds to cover existing spending commitments. Given the limited time, Congress and the White House may be compelled to agree to a relatively small, short-term increase in the debt ceiling, potentially covering only a few months. This compromise, coupled with previously agreed-upon cuts, would provide leaders with more time to negotiate substantial budget reforms, including possible adjustments to entitlement programs like Medicare and Medicaid. However, Obama expressed opposition to a short-term increase, stating, "I don't think the American people sent us here to avoid tough problems." Obama described the debt ceiling dispute as a "unique opportunity to do something big" and "put the economy on a stronger footing for the future." Over the weekend, leading Democrats and Republicans offered no public indication of a potential compromise. Talks led by Vice President Joe Biden recently broke down over the tax issue. "The principle of not raising taxes is something that we campaigned on last November, and the results of the election was the American people don't want their taxes raised and they wanted us to cut spending," Sen. John McCain, R-Arizona, said Sunday on CNN's "State of the Union." "They don't want compromise." Various proposals for a potential agreement have been suggested. Conservatives demand substantial spending cuts, caps on future spending, and a balanced budget amendment to the U.S. Constitution in exchange for their support to raise the debt ceiling. Both the House and Senate are planning votes on a balanced budget amendment in the coming weeks. However, given that such an amendment requires approval from a two-thirds majority in both chambers and ratification by at least 38 states, its eventual approval remains uncertain in a process that could take years. For his part, Obama has criticized congressional Republicans for refusing to make "tough decisions" that might be unpopular with their conservative base. He advocates for what he calls a balanced approach to deficit reduction, including increased revenue for education, infrastructure, and clean energy—areas he believes are critical to long-term economic growth. The Democratic position includes spending cuts in other areas, such as the military, as well as reforms to entitlement programs like Medicare and Medicaid, which provide government-run health care to senior citizens, the disabled, and the indigent. Republicans are seeking more extensive entitlement reforms that Democrats argue would undermine the safety net these programs are intended to provide. CNN's Tom Cohen, Alan Silverleib, Kate Bolduan and Ted Barrett contributed to this report. Watch State of the Union with Candy Crowley Sundays at 9am ET. translated_content: Il Presidente Barack Obama ha annunciato martedì di aver invitato i leader democratici e repubblicani di entrambe le Camere del Congresso a un incontro alla Casa Bianca giovedì. L'obiettivo è discutere la riduzione del deficit e la necessità di innalzare il tetto del debito federale. Obama ha dichiarato di volere che l'incontro "costruisca sul lavoro già svolto e conduca a un accordo finale". Questo accordo affronterebbe l'espansione dei deficit federali e assicurerebbe l'approvazione del Congresso per l'aumento del limite di prestito del governo. Il leader della minoranza al Senato, Mitch McConnell, che in precedenza aveva invitato Obama a rivolgersi al Congresso sulla questione, parteciperà all'incontro alla Casa Bianca, secondo quanto riferito dal suo ufficio. Anche il leader della maggioranza al Senato, Harry Reid, prevede di partecipare. Il Presidente della Camera, John Boehner, ha indicato la sua partecipazione, ma ha avvertito che il Congresso respingerà gli aumenti delle tasse richiesti da Obama e dai Democratici. "Sono felice di discutere queste questioni alla Casa Bianca, ma tali discussioni saranno infruttuose finché il presidente non riconoscerà la realtà economica e legislativa", ha detto Boehner, repubblicano dell'Ohio, in una dichiarazione. Ha aggiunto: "Sono lieto che il presidente abbia dichiarato oggi che dobbiamo affrontare le grandi sfide a lungo termine che il nostro Paese si trova ad affrontare." Obama, in un'apparizione non programmata nella sala stampa della Casa Bianca, ha affermato che i colloqui sulla riduzione del deficit con i leader del Congresso durante il fine settimana del Quattro Luglio hanno mostrato progressi, ma che "dobbiamo ancora superare alcune reali divergenze". Obama ha esortato entrambe le parti a uscire dalla loro loro "zona di comfort", sottolineando che "questo non dovrebbe ridursi all'ultimo secondo". Il portavoce della Casa Bianca, Jay Carney, ha poi espresso la convinzione di Obama che le questioni coinvolte nel raggiungimento di un accordo globale per ridurre i deficit federali fino a 4.000 miliardi di dollari nel prossimo decennio siano ben comprese. Carney ha affermato che è ora di prendere decisioni difficili, con entrambe le parti che si impegnano a trovare un accordo vantaggioso per l'intera nazione. "L'ideale non diventerà mai legge, che tu sia un repubblicano conservatore della Camera, un democratico liberale o il presidente degli Stati Uniti", ha dichiarato Carney. "Non otterrai mai tutto ciò che vuoi, perché il nostro sistema non funziona così." Il Senato si è riunito martedì, interrompendo la pausa di una settimana prevista per il Quattro Luglio, con i leader che hanno ripreso le discussioni sui negoziati sul deficit federale in vista dell'imminente scadenza per innalzare il tetto del debito del governo. Il fine settimana del Quattro Luglio, durato tre giorni, non ha fatto molto per alterare la retorica che circonda i colloqui sulla riduzione del deficit e la necessità per il Congresso di aumentare la capacità di prestito del governo. Nelle sue osservazioni di apertura dopo la riconvocazione del Senato, Reid, democratico del Nevada, ha accusato i repubblicani di mettere a rischio la ripresa economica della nazione minacciando di opporsi a un aumento del limite di prestito del governo. McConnell, repubblicano del Kentucky, ha risposto accusando i democratici di cercare un aumento della spesa come soluzione al problema del deficit. Prima dell'invito di Obama, McConnell ha ribadito il suo invito a Obama a rivolgersi al Congresso e ad ascoltare le preoccupazioni dei repubblicani su qualsiasi accordo che coinvolga aumenti delle tasse. Reid ha dichiarato la disponibilità del suo partito a scendere a compromessi, ma ha respinto gli sforzi dei repubblicani per dare la priorità agli interessi di "alcuni milionari e miliardari" rispetto a quelli della popolazione più ampia. Con i membri della Camera previsti per il ritorno mercoledì, i leader del Congresso rimangono fortemente divisi sulle condizioni da allegare a un aumento dell'attuale tetto del debito di 14.300 miliardi di dollari. I repubblicani insistono su profondi tagli alla spesa e sull'esclusione degli aumenti delle tasse come precondizioni per qualsiasi aumento. I democratici stanno cercando di minimizzare i tagli ai servizi sociali e sostengono l'eliminazione di specifiche agevolazioni fiscali e scappatoie a vantaggio degli americani più ricchi. I funzionari del Dipartimento del Tesoro e i principali economisti hanno avvertito di potenziali conseguenze catastrofiche se il tetto del debito non verrà innalzato entro il 2 agosto, il che potrebbe portare a un default sugli obblighi del debito della nazione. Un tale default potrebbe innescare un'impennata dei tassi di interesse e un crollo del dollaro, tra gli altri effetti negativi. L'aumento del tetto del debito consentirebbe al governo di prendere in prestito fondi aggiuntivi per coprire gli impegni di spesa esistenti. Dato il tempo limitato, il Congresso e la Casa Bianca potrebbero essere costretti ad accettare un aumento relativamente piccolo e a breve termine del tetto del debito, potenzialmente coprendo solo pochi mesi. Questo compromesso, unito a tagli precedentemente concordati, fornirebbe ai leader più tempo per negoziare riforme di bilancio sostanziali, inclusi possibili adeguamenti ai programmi di assistenza come Medicare e Medicaid. Tuttavia, Obama ha espresso opposizione a un aumento a breve termine, affermando: "Non penso che il popolo americano ci abbia mandato qui per evitare problemi difficili". Obama ha descritto la disputa sul tetto del debito come una "opportunità unica per fare qualcosa di grande" e "mettere l'economia su una base più solida per il futuro". Durante il fine settimana, i principali democratici e repubblicani non hanno offerto alcuna indicazione pubblica di un potenziale compromesso. I colloqui guidati dal vicepresidente Joe Biden si sono recentemente interrotti sulla questione fiscale. "Il principio di non aumentare le tasse è qualcosa su cui abbiamo fatto campagna lo scorso novembre e il risultato delle elezioni è stato che il popolo americano non vuole che le sue tasse vengano aumentate e voleva che tagliassimo la spesa", ha detto domenica il senatore John McCain, repubblicano dell'Arizona, su "State of the Union" della CNN. "Non vogliono compromessi." Sono state suggerite varie proposte per un potenziale accordo. I conservatori chiedono sostanziali tagli alla spesa, limiti alla spesa futura e un emendamento per il bilancio in pareggio alla Costituzione degli Stati Uniti in cambio del loro sostegno all'innalzamento del tetto del debito. Sia la Camera che il Senato stanno pianificando votazioni su un emendamento per il bilancio in pareggio nelle prossime settimane. Tuttavia, dato che tale emendamento richiede l'approvazione da parte di una maggioranza di due terzi in entrambe le Camere e la ratifica da parte di almeno 38 Stati, la sua eventuale approvazione rimane incerta in un processo che potrebbe richiedere anni. Da parte sua, Obama ha criticato i repubblicani del Congresso per aver rifiutato di prendere "decisioni difficili" che potrebbero essere impopolari tra la loro base conservatrice. Sostiene quello che chiama un approccio equilibrato alla riduzione del deficit, compresi maggiori entrate per l'istruzione, le infrastrutture e l'energia pulita, aree che ritiene fondamentali per la crescita economica a lungo termine. La posizione democratica include tagli alla spesa in altre aree, come quella militare, nonché riforme ai programmi di assistenza come Medicare e Medicaid, che forniscono assistenza sanitaria gestita dal governo agli anziani, ai disabili e agli indigenti. I repubblicani stanno cercando riforme di assistenza più ampie che, secondo i democratici, minerebbero la rete di sicurezza che questi programmi intendono fornire. Tom Cohen, Alan Silverleib, Kate Bolduan e Ted Barrett della CNN hanno contribuito a questo rapporto. Guarda State of the Union con Candy Crowley la domenica alle 9 del mattino ET. article_content: On Thursday, March 21, 2013, a severe blizzard sweeping across the Canadian plains led to a massive pileup on Highway 2, south of Edmonton, Alberta. The treacherous conditions resulted in over one hundred injuries and left numerous people stranded in their vehicles for hours. By 4 p.m., emergency responders had transported twenty-two individuals to local hospitals: one in critical condition, seven with moderate injuries, and fourteen with minor ones, according to Alberta Health Services. Approximately eighty more received treatment at the scene of the accident. Initial reports had estimated around 300 injuries with four serious ones, but this number was later revised. The collision, which involved a passenger bus, semi-trailer trucks, and numerous cars, occurred just before noon and forced the closure of Highway 2 for several hours. Derek Fildebrandt, a passenger on the bus, described the scene to the Edmonton Journal: 'I looked up and eighteen-wheelers were crashing into each other, cars flying into each other. It was a pileup roughly every 200 meters.' Crews faced significant challenges clearing the road due to a substantial snowdrift, estimated to be 100 meters long and over half a meter deep. Fire officials and a 'multi-casualty' incident bus responded to the scene, checking on passengers in each vehicle, according to Kerry Williamson from Alberta Health Services. Many injured individuals were transported to hospitals in nearby communities such as Edmonton and Red Deer. Whiteout conditions exacerbated the situation, and the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) closed a portion of Highway 2, the primary route connecting Edmonton and Calgary, redirecting traffic away from the site of the collision, stated RCMP Staff Sgt. Grant MacDonald. Between 6 a.m. and 5 p.m. that day, Edmonton police reported an overwhelming 133 traffic accidents. This was a significant increase from their average daily count of 50 to 70 crashes, nine of which resulted in injuries, nine involved hit-and-run incidents, and 115 involved minor damages.

article_content: Footage has surfaced showing the heartwarming birth of a bottlenose dolphin at a zoo in Chicago. The video captures the poignant moment when the mother assisted her newborn in swimming to the water's surface for its initial breath. The latest addition to Brookfield Zoo arrived around 11 a.m. last Friday. This occurred approximately two hours after Allie, the 26-year-old mother, began exhibiting labor signs. In the video, Allie can be seen gracefully moving through the water. Another dolphin from the pod attentively observes as the calf is born tail first. The other dolphin seemingly assisted in the delivery as the calf emerged. Though the 3-foot calf was born at a healthy 40 pounds, the subsequent month is crucial for both the young dolphin and its mother. Beyond documenting the birth, the footage showcases the tender moments after, illustrating the bottlenose dolphin forming a connection with her calf and providing nourishment. The calf was also allowed to relax in her slipstream. The mother will nurse the calf for approximately 18 months, producing milk that, according to SeaWorld, boasts the consistency of a milkshake. Later, the calf will be taught how to hunt fish. At Brookfield Zoo, a bottlenose dolphin recently gave birth to a female calf. The 40-pound, 3-foot calf was born on August 2 at the zoo and appears healthy. 'We're currently heartened by Allie and the calf's behavior,' noted Rita Stacey from the Chicago Zoological Society. 'However, we're staying carefully hopeful because the calf's first 30 days are very important.' Allie has been under careful observation since becoming pregnant a year ago, with routine ultrasounds monitoring the unborn calf's development. Tapeko, another female dolphin at the zoo who has previously delivered several calves and is expecting another later this year, kept Allie company during labor. While the new mother and calf adjust, the zoo has temporarily closed the dolphin exhibit. Newborn calves need assistance reaching the surface to breathe and require regular feeding from their mothers. It will take some time before the newest member of the pod makes her public debut. Sondra Katzen told the Chicago Tribune, 'We're definitely excited.' The calf, yet to be named, will eventually join her mother and the other bottlenose dolphins at Brookfield Zoo’s Seven Seas exhibit as she grows older. The bottlenose dolphin and her calf are reportedly doing well, but those initial 30 days remain critical.

article_content: By Daniel Miller PUBLISHED: 06:13 EST, 15 August 2012 | UPDATED: 19:09 EST, 15 August 2012 A devoted mother was stabbed to death by her ‘wicked and callous’ former partner who could not accept that she wanted to reconcile with her husband for the sake of her children. Jeanette Goodwin, 47, ended her long-term relationship with Martin Bunch, 44, and returned to her husband of 21 years, Mark. The couple were at home preparing a barbecue when Bunch forced his way into the garden through a gap in the fence and launched the fatal attack. Mrs. Goodwin bled to death on her patio after a 5-inch blade was plunged into her chest more than 20 times as Bunch exclaimed: ‘I told her I would kill her.’ Guilty: Martin Bunch (left) stabbed to death his former lover Jeanette Goodwin (right) after she broke off their eight-year affair to rebuild her marriage. At the time, he was under a restraining order, prohibiting him from contacting his ex-partner or going to her house in Southend, following his arrest for harassing her. He remained free despite repeatedly breaching the conditions, and the mother of three informed police that she had been told he planned to kill her. Bunch was found guilty of murder after a four-week trial at Chelmsford Crown Court and faces a mandatory life sentence when he is sentenced on Friday. Horror: Mrs. Goodwin's husband, Mark Goodwin, witnessed the attack in which his wife was stabbed multiple times with a five-inch kitchen knife. Judge Charles Gratwicke said: ‘This was a wicked, callous, and violent crime for which he has shown absolutely no remorse whatsoever. He should expect a really substantial prison sentence.’ Mr. and Mrs. Goodwin married in 1990. They had three children – Samantha, 21, Charles, 18, and Harry, 14 – but their marriage went through a rough patch, and they separated. Mrs. Goodwin began an eight-year relationship with Bunch which ended in late 2010 when she told him she was going to try to reconcile with her husband. The labourer began bombarding her with calls and was charged with harassment. Magistrates released him on bail after imposing the restraining order, but less than a month before her death, Mrs. Goodwin told police she had received unwanted voicemails, texts, and visits from Bunch, who had also told his mother he planned to kill her. She said: ‘This behavior has left me fearful for my life. I just want him to leave me alone.’ Bunch was arrested again on July 14 for removing a tag used to check he was observing a curfew, but on July 20 he was again granted bail at Southend Magistrates’ Court. Four days later, Mrs. Goodwin saw him outside her home. She did not report it to police immediately because she refused to let him spoil a ‘lovely summer’s afternoon’. At around 7:30 pm, she pressed a panic alarm. Police arrived six minutes later, but she had already been stabbed. Her children were not at home at the time. Bunch, of Southend, was found at his mother’s house 30 minutes later clutching a 5-inch kitchen knife. He denied murder, claiming he did not remember what happened, but was found guilty by a unanimous verdict on Tuesday. Investigation: A forensic tent in the back garden of Mark and Jeanette's family home where she was found collapsed on the ground.

article_content: Eugenie Bouchard defeated Simona Halep 7-6, 6-2 on Centre Court to become the first Canadian ever to reach a Grand Slam singles final. Her achievement has been widely celebrated in Canada. In addition to being the top sports story in Canada, sports teams, prominent figures, and stars have paid tribute to the 20-year-old's historic run at Wimbledon. NHL ice hockey teams like the Montreal Canadiens and Calgary Flames, as well as Prime Minister Stephen Harper, tweeted their congratulations to the No. 13 seed. Historic milestone: Eugenie Bouchard is the first Canadian to reach a Grand Slam singles final. Aiming for victory: Bouchard will compete against Petra Kvitova in the Wimbledon final on Saturday. The Montreal Canadiens NHL team shared an image of Bouchard wearing their jersey last year. The Canadian Football League also acknowledged the 20-year-old's achievement. Tennis Canada shared a video on YouTube showing their reaction to match point, thanking fans for their support and expressing that they were 'speechless'. Sochi 2014 Olympic ski cross gold medalist Marielle Thompson also commended Bouchard for making history, and Justin Trudeau, a member of the Canadian House of Commons, called her a phenomenal Canadian athlete. Toronto Sun sports columnist Steve Simmons commented: 'A Canadian. In our lifetime. For the first time. Amazing,' while Canadian journalist Sandra Prusina predicted Bouchard would win the Championships. Bouchard will face 2011 champion Petra Kvitova in the final on Saturday. Her family, including her twin sister Beatrice, are traveling to London to watch the 20-year-old compete for the Wimbledon title.

article_content: Rolf Harris, after being sentenced, was reportedly fast-tracked to a 'soft' prison in Oxfordshire, bypassing a stay at the tougher Wandsworth Prison, leading to suggestions of preferential treatment. The disgraced entertainer was expected to be held at Wandsworth Prison in south-west London following his sentence of five years and nine months for multiple sex attacks. However, the 84-year-old was immediately taken to HMP Bullingdon in Oxfordshire after his conviction for 12 indecent assaults, sparking speculation about special treatment. Concerns have been raised about the length of Harris's prison sentence. He could be released in under three years, and Attorney General Jeremy Wright will investigate its perceived leniency following public complaints. Initially, it was believed Harris was placed in a healthcare unit at Wandsworth Prison, where fellow convicted paedophile Max Clifford was also held after his own sentencing for indecent assault. The expectation was for Harris to spend several weeks at Wandsworth for assessment before any potential transfer. However, it's now reported that Harris never spent a night in the category B prison but was instead taken to Bullingdon, a category B/C prison near Bicester known for its work with older inmates. A source told The People that it's unusual for prisoners to begin their sentence at Bullingdon, as transfers typically occur later as a reward for good behavior. 'If you're convicted of a serious crime at Southwark Crown Court, you're generally sent to Wandsworth, without exception,' the source stated. Bullingdon, which opened in 1995, holds approximately 1,000 prisoners, compared to Wandsworth's 1,900. Wandsworth, built during the Victorian era, once housed inmates like Charles Bronson, Great Train Robber Ronnie Biggs, and Ronnie Kray. Former Energy Secretary Chris Huhne also began his sentence at Wandsworth after being sentenced at Southwark Crown Court, before being transferred to HMP Leyhill in Gloucestershire. The source suggested Harris's placement in a smaller institution might be to facilitate easier observation by guards and prevent potential attacks from other inmates. Another source told The Sunday Mirror that Harris shares a cell at Bullingdon with another elderly inmate and has become very withdrawn. 'He is doing okay but spends much time drawing. It distracts him,' the source added. A Ministry of Justice spokesman told MailOnline that the department does not comment on the whereabouts of individual prisoners and cannot comment on standard procedures following sentencing at Southwark Crown Court. Harris was sentenced earlier in the month, having travelled part of the way to Southwark from his home in Bray, Berkshire, by boat, where he was observed joking with friends. He showed no emotion when Mr Justice Sweeney described him as a committed sex offender who exploited his celebrity status to assault four women, aged between eight and 19, in public view between 1969 and 1986. Following victim impact statements, the court heard that his daughter Bindi’s best friend, who was abused from age 13, felt ‘dirty, grubby and disgusting’, and another woman said Harris stole her innocence at age eight. 'You exploited the trust placed in you due to your celebrity to commit these offenses,' the judge told Harris. 'You clearly enjoyed committing the offenses in the presence of others or nearby. ‘You have shown no remorse for your crimes at all. 'Your reputation is now ruined, you have been stripped of your honors, and you have no one to blame but yourself.’ It was alleged that Harris possessed child pornography on his home computer, depicting children under 13 naked from the waist down, posing suggestively with teddy bears. He was charged with making indecent images, but prosecutors dropped the charges to avoid appearing ‘oppressive’ towards the sexual predator, who was purportedly living on borrowed time. Harris was convicted of 12 counts of indecent assault after an eight-week trial that revealed the hidden dark side of his personality. He concealed the ‘demon lurking beneath his charming exterior’ and used his fame to manipulate innocent young fans. Since his conviction, several other women in Australia and New Zealand have come forward with claims of molestation. Singer Linda Nolan, 55, and television presenter Vanessa Feltz, 52, have also alleged they were assaulted by Harris. Feltz stated Harris put his hands up her dress during a live broadcast of The Big Breakfast in 1996, while Nolan claimed Harris attacked her when she was 15 during a tour of South Africa.

Inizialmente, si credeva che Harris fosse stato posto in un'unità sanitaria nel carcere di Wandsworth, dove anche il compagno pedofilo condannato Max Clifford era detenuto dopo la sua condanna per aggressione indecente. Ci si aspettava che Harris trascorresse diverse settimane a Wandsworth per una valutazione prima di un eventuale trasferimento. Tuttavia, è stato riferito che Harris non ha mai trascorso una notte nella prigione di categoria B, ma è stato invece portato a Bullingdon, una prigione di categoria B/C vicino a Bicester, nota per il suo lavoro con detenuti anziani. Una fonte ha riferito a The People che è insolito che i prigionieri inizino la loro pena a Bullingdon, poiché i trasferimenti di solito avvengono in seguito come ricompensa per buona condotta. 'Se sei condannato per un crimine grave alla Southwark Crown Court, di solito vieni mandato a Wandsworth, senza eccezioni,' ha dichiarato la fonte. Bullingdon, inaugurato nel 1995, ospita circa 1.000 prigionieri, rispetto ai 1.900 di Wandsworth. Wandsworth, costruito in epoca vittoriana, un tempo ospitava detenuti come Charles Bronson, il rapinatore del Grande Treno Ronnie Biggs e Ronnie Kray. Anche l'ex Segretario all'Energia Chris Huhne ha iniziato la sua pena a Wandsworth dopo essere stato condannato alla Southwark Crown Court, prima di essere trasferito all'HMP Leyhill, nel Gloucestershire. La fonte ha suggerito che il trasferimento di Harris in un istituto più piccolo potrebbe essere volto a facilitare l'osservazione da parte delle guardie e prevenire potenziali aggressioni da parte di altri detenuti. Un'altra fonte ha riferito a The Sunday Mirror che Harris condivide una cella a Bullingdon con un altro detenuto anziano e si è isolato molto. 'Sta bene, ma passa molto tempo a disegnare. Lo distrae,' ha aggiunto la fonte. Un portavoce del Ministero della Giustizia ha dichiarato a MailOnline che il dipartimento non commenta la posizione dei singoli prigionieri e non può commentare le procedure standard a seguito di una condanna alla Southwark Crown Court. Harris è stato condannato all'inizio del mese, dopo aver viaggiato in parte verso Southwark dalla sua casa a Bray, nel Berkshire, in barca, dove è stato visto scherzare con degli amici. Non ha mostrato alcuna emozione quando il giudice Sweeney lo ha descritto come un molestatore seriale che ha sfruttato la sua fama per aggredire quattro donne, di età compresa tra gli otto e i 19 anni, pubblicamente tra il 1969 e il 1986. A seguito delle testimonianze delle vittime, il tribunale ha appreso che la migliore amica di sua figlia Bindi, che ha subito abusi dall'età di 13 anni, si sentiva 'sporca, sporca e disgustosa', e un'altra donna ha affermato che Harris le ha rubato l'innocenza all'età di otto anni. 'Hai sfruttato la fiducia che ti era stata data a causa della tua celebrità per commettere questi reati,' ha detto il giudice Harris. 'Ti è chiaramente piaciuto commettere i reati in presenza di altre persone o nelle vicinanze. ‘Non hai mostrato alcun rimorso per i tuoi crimini. 'La tua reputazione è ormai distrutta, sei stato privato dei tuoi onori e non hai nessuno da incolpare se non te stesso.’ È stato affermato che Harris possedeva materiale pedopornografico sul suo computer di casa, che raffigurava bambini di età inferiore ai 13 anni nudi dalla vita in giù, in posa in modo provocante con orsacchiotti. È stato accusato di aver prodotto immagini indecenti, ma i pubblici ministeri hanno ritirato le accuse per evitare di apparire 'oppressivi' nei confronti del predatore sessuale, che si diceva stesse vivendo gli ultimi giorni. Harris è stato condannato per 12 capi di imputazione per aggressione indecente dopo un processo durato otto settimane che ha rivelato il lato oscuro nascosto della sua personalità. Ha nascosto il 'demone in agguato sotto il suo affascinante aspetto' e ha usato la sua fama per manipolare giovani fan innocenti. Dopo la sua condanna, molte altre donne in Australia e Nuova Zelanda si sono fatte avanti con accuse di molestie. La cantante Linda Nolan, 55 anni, e la conduttrice televisiva Vanessa Feltz, 52 anni, hanno anche affermato di essere state aggredite da Harris. Feltz ha dichiarato che Harris le ha messo le mani sotto il vestito durante una trasmissione in diretta di The Big Breakfast nel 1996, mentre Nolan ha affermato che Harris l'ha aggredita quando aveva 15 anni durante un tour in Sud Africa.

article_content: By Jennifer Smith. This is the dramatic moment a college student's car burst into flames shortly after she escaped. The incident occurred just yards from a petrol station in North Cheam, Surrey, yesterday morning, after the student smelled burning plastic. When smoke began to fill the front of the car, the student ran out onto the side of the A217, where she watched the vehicle become engulfed in flames. Scroll down for video. The student is lucky to be alive after fleeing her car moments before it burst into flames on a busy road. No one was injured in the incident near St Dunstan's Hill; however, the student lost several college assignments that were in her back seat. Firefighter Ray Foster said: 'The student was driving, and she had the heater on in her car. After a while, she started to smell burning plastic, and then smoke started coming through the passenger compartment. 'She got out of the car, and it was engulfed in flames.' Mr. Foster added the blaze was so severe that the car's engine fell out. 'She was a college student, and all her assignments were in the car, plus £200 worth of make-up.' Firefighters were able to put out the blaze on the A217 near St Dunstan's Hill in Surrey yesterday morning. The student was collected by a family friend (pictured) after firefighters were able to retrieve her house keys and make-up from the ruined car. Amazingly, firefighters were able to retrieve the student's make-up bag and house keys, which were both intact. A local resident watched the incident unfold from a window in her nearby home. Jacqueline Salerno said: 'All of a sudden, within two seconds, there was an explosion. 'But luckily, no one was passing by. 'The student driving got out in time - I would say four seconds before the explosion.' New Malden firefighters said the student was understandably 'shaken up' by the incident, which could have taken her life.

article_content: SpaghettiOs made a faux pas on the 72nd anniversary of Japan's attack on the Pearl Harbor naval base when it decided to commemorate the event by tweeting a photo of its grinning mascot with an American flag. 'Take a moment to remember #PearlHarbor with us,' read the tweet last Friday night. Pearl Harbor commemorates the death of 2,386 Americans and is a national tragedy. The photo of a smiling pasta-O holding an American flag drew criticism and sparked outrage. The company's attempt to promote SpaghettiOs with a cheerful image during a tragic remembrance drew considerable attention on Twitter. 'Hope nobody minds if I chose to remember Pearl Harbor and forever forget @SpaghettiOs. #TastelessCorporation,' said Twitter user Laura. 'I can't wait for the official @spaghettiOs 9/11 tweet,' said Suzan Eraslan. '@SpaghettiOs maybe sit out the next couple plays,' said Andy Levy. After realizing the offense caused, SpaghettiOs issued a formal apology on December 7. 'We apologize for our recent tweet in remembrance of Pearl Harbor Day. We meant to pay respect, not to offend.' Marketingland.com reported that the offensive tweet received over 3,000 retweets, primarily driven by outrage rather than popularity. SpaghettiOs issued a formal apology on December 7 and deleted the original post. According to thinkprogress.org, this is not the first time corporations have attempted to use public holidays to promote their brand, even when considered inappropriate. On Veterans' Day, the movie Man of Steel tweeted a picture of the film along with a 'thank you to the troops' message. The brand Kenneth Cole tweeted during the revolutionary uprising in Egypt, stating, 'Millions are in uproar in #Cairo. Rumor is they heard our new Spring collection is available online.' SpaghettiOs, an American brand under the Campbell's Soup umbrella, features circular pasta covered in a cheese and tomato sauce. It is packaged in a can and marketed to parents as 'less messy' than regular pasta. If only the same could be said about their 'messy' advertising practices.

article_content: George Michael revealed he rarely left his cell during his prison sentence, a traumatic period where he claims he was housed alongside paedophiles. The singer served half of an eight-week sentence at HMP Pentonville in North London and Highpoint Prison in Suffolk after crashing his car into a shop while under the influence of cannabis three years prior. He described Pentonville, a Category B jail, as a 'horrific' experience in September 2010, before being transferred to Highpoint, a Category C prison known for its more relaxed environment. Speaking to BBC Radio 2, Michael, 50, said Pentonville was 'really quite a horrific experience' and that he was placed 'with the paedophiles and the bullied', leading him to stay in his cell most of the time. The former Wham! star added that the car crash served as a turning point in his sobriety: 'From the moment that last crash happened (I started to get sober) - because apart from anything else, I realised it had to be something to do with me.' 'It shook me out of my denial in a way that the others hadn’t, probably because there was a chance I’d go to prison. So from the day after that crash happened, I started in drug counselling.' He mentioned spending two weeks in detox privately and expressed that his issues with illegal drugs 'feel so completely behind me'. Michael also shared his decision to end his 13-year relationship with Kenny Goss and noted that his jail time sparked a 'burst of creativity', resulting in the creation of eight songs in less than three weeks. Upon his release from jail in October 2010, Michael expressed a desire to 'start again' and engage more openly with the press, stating, 'You'll get sick of me. You'll see me about.' He described his freedom as 'fantastic', expressed his eagerness to 'go out', and thanked those who supported him during his incarceration, calling it 'quite inspirational'. Michael was jailed in September 2010 after admitting to driving while unfit through drugs and possessing cannabis cigarettes at Highbury Corner Magistrates' Court. He served the remaining four weeks of his sentence on license, paid £1,365 in fines and costs, and received a five-year driving ban. He denied receiving preferential treatment at Highpoint, where he was held in the good behaviour unit, which houses the most trusted inmates. Michael spent three nights in Pentonville before being transferred to Highpoint, nicknamed 'Hi-de-Highpoint' due to its easy-going regime. During the Radio 2 interview, Michael also revealed that he battled pneumonia mid-way through a concert schedule three years prior and has sold 120 million records.

article_content: While medications often bring unwelcome side effects like headaches or weight fluctuations, one Californian teen's experience was particularly striking. Jena Graves, a 19-year-old from Napa, faced significant weight gain after starting medication for Lupus, a condition diagnosed at 15 that compromises the immune system. Before her diagnosis, Jena was a vibrant and active teen, standing 5'2" and enjoying softball, as she shared with the San Francisco Chronicle. However, her treatment involved a combination of 25 drugs, including prednisone. Prednisone, while controlling autoimmune disorders, is known to increase appetite and promote fat retention. Over five years, Jena's weight more than doubled from 120lbs to 272lbs. The family wasn't informed about these potential side effects, leading Jena to constantly eat, often consuming junk food in an attempt to satisfy her persistent hunger. She recounted how she would frequently eat from the fridge, especially when her mother wasn't home. This weight gain took a toll, causing exhaustion and depression, preventing her from playing softball and socializing. Jena eventually withdrew from seventh grade at Redwood Middle School and took classes in the hospital instead. Despite these challenges, she later graduated from Vintage High School. Her mother, Mindy, initially trusted the doctors' decisions, but Jena's condition worsened. She developed Type 2 diabetes, possibly triggered by the drugs' impact on her blood sugar levels. Jena then started metformin to regulate her glucose levels. In 2009, seeking a second opinion at Stanford, doctors reduced Jena's prednisone dosage and discontinued most of her other medications. They also discovered that prednisone had weakened her bones, causing a back fracture. Dr. John Morton at Stanford Hospital performed gastric bypass surgery, which helped Jena manage her weight. She is now healthier, having lost 40lbs and transitioned to azathioprine for Lupus management. Dr. Morton emphasized the importance of carefully considering the appropriateness of prescribing obesity-generating drugs widely.

article_content: On Thursday, pirates hijacked a German-owned tanker in the Gulf of Aden, a waterway between Africa and the Middle East that has become one of the world's most dangerous shipping lanes. The U.S. Navy, along with other countries, is patrolling the Gulf of Aden. The MV Longchamp was seized by seven pirates early in the morning, according to a spokesman for the ship's owner, Bernhard Schulte Ship Management Company, based in Hamburg, Germany. The company received a very brief phone call from the ship's captain, lasting only about three seconds. The captain reported that they had been seized by pirates, that there were no injuries or fatalities, and then the call abruptly ended,' the spokesman said, withholding his name. He added that the company had not received any communication from the pirates and had no information on how the vessel was seized. Lt. Nathan Christensen, a public affairs officer for the U.S. Navy's Fifth Fleet, based in the region, stated that the coalition of countries patrolling the sea lanes in response to piracy was not involved in the incident. He said he did not know if the coalition had received a distress call from the Longchamp. The Longchamp has a crew of 12 Filipinos and one Indonesian, Christensen noted. The tanker is carrying the chemical vinyl chloride monomer (VCM), the owner's spokesman confirmed.

article_content: Des Moines, Iowa (CNN) -- Hillary Clinton's potential decision not to run for president might be influenced by a return to the intense media spotlight. Despite her national book tour and paid lectures, Clinton experienced the current frenzied political news environment firsthand during her first Iowa visit in seven years. This event was primed for significant media coverage due to her speculated campaign and complex history with Iowa. I was among over 200 reporters who attended, actively tweeting, though many social media users were likely more interested in other topics. The press gathering to see Hillary and Bill Clinton, neither of whom are candidates, flipping Hy-Vee steaks with Sen. Tom Harkin—behind a barricade—rivaled the media presence during her peak 2008 campaign. One reporter was hit by a television camera, and a photographer fell from his ladder. The scene was somewhat absurd. When the Clintons engaged with the media, Bill Clinton seemed to enjoy it, while Hillary remained reserved. Political Twitter featured both images of the Clintons and criticism of the media, some justified, labeling the event as 'pack journalism' with limited journalistic merit. This criticism held some weight. What advantage did being one of many reporters there offer, all competing for the same quotes and images? This was particularly true for journalists who rarely cover politics outside of Washington or New York. Would their time have been better spent covering underreported Senate or governor's races elsewhere? Academics might agree, but the click-driven news economy favors Hillary over lesser-known figures like Arkansas' Tom Cotton. While I advocate avoiding the media pack—a key point in my Harvard Kennedy School study, 'Did Twitter Kill The Boys on the Bus?'—I found value in covering the Steak Fry. Having closely followed Clinton's 2008 campaign as an embedded CNN producer, I observed whether her political skills and engagement with Iowa had changed since her loss to Barack Obama. While the event was broadcast on CNN and C-SPAN, reporters on the ground could discern subtleties, like the crowd's receptiveness, the Ready for Hillary super PAC's organizational strength, the staged photo-ops, and Clinton's cautious body language compared to Bill. My reporting focused on these atmospherics and discussions with Democrat and Republican sources in Des Moines. Was the trip worth it? Absolutely. Will my next trip involve less crowded venues? Definitely. Watching the Iowa theatrics from afar, journalist Dave Weigel noted that Hillary's potential candidacy presents a 'problem for the media,' which is both ready to cover her extensively and yet 'palpably bored' with her approach. The press, amplified by Twitter, will challenge Clinton, who must engage with numerous reporters seeking 'news'—anything noteworthy or click-worthy—while controlling her message. Mitt Romney faced similar challenges. Avoiding the press led to criticism, while policy-focused press conferences were overshadowed by irrelevant questions or Twitter controversies. He opted for direct communication through paid media and friendly interviews on Fox News. Ultimately, this wasn't enough. While political reporters are drawn to conflict and campaign dynamics, the atomized social news environment has significantly changed since Clinton's 2007 campaign, before the widespread adoption of iPhones and Twitter. Reporters covering her now might have grown up in the age of Internet journalism, prioritizing exclusives and micronews, with different incentives than previous generations. While respecting the Clintons, their regard isn't as high as the Clintons' self-regard. Clinton experienced this during her book tour, where controversial comments quickly spread online. The Iowa visit offered a glimpse into the challenges ahead.

article_content: In 2010, Google launched a short-lived social network service called 'Buzz'. Instead of simply promoting Buzz and urging users to sign up or opt in, Google signed up Gmail users as Buzz users by default. Users who were unhappy could opt out. This caused issues. Private email addresses became publicly available as social network contacts, leading to user backlash. The Federal Trade Commission investigated, Google relented, and eventually, the company settled with the FTC and agreed not to enroll users in new services without their consent. Now, Google is repeating similar behavior. This week, the company announced that it was linking the inboxes of Gmail users to Google+ profiles. By using Gmail addresses to autocomplete messages from Google+ users, Google allows strangers, who may not have your email address, to connect with you through Gmail. This move might increase Google's short-term value but reduces privacy for Gmail users. This announcement is partially driven by the ongoing competition with Facebook, but also by Google's increasing integration of user data across its various internet services. This trend began when Google revised its privacy policy for Gmail and other Google products, enabling them to target more advertising and enhance user profiling. The consequences for users and the internet are concerning. From a privacy standpoint, Google's action increases the likelihood that users' personal information will become more widely accessible. As the internet's most dominant company, Google is leveraging its control over key internet services to suppress competition and expand its market reach. Those who advocate for a free, open, and democratic internet should take note. Google is unfairly expecting Gmail users to opt out of a service they never requested to maintain their existing privacy expectations. While some users might appreciate the new feature and should be free to opt in, those who value privacy should not be required to constantly check their privacy settings whenever a company changes its business model. With this latest change to Gmail, Google is testing the resolve of regulators to protect privacy. If government officials do not intervene, the situation could worsen. Currently, Google is using Gmail account addresses to autocomplete email addresses for Google+. However, Google possesses the largest search database globally and could potentially use the data collected from users to autocomplete email addresses and more. In 2010, Google appropriately retracted its plan for Buzz, and the Federal Trade Commission rightly investigated and helped prevent similar occurrences. Now that Google is again commingling data in email accounts and social network accounts, the Federal Trade Commission needs to intervene. Opting out is not a sufficient solution.

Attualmente, Google utilizza gli indirizzi degli account Gmail per completare automaticamente gli indirizzi email per Google+. Tuttavia, Google possiede il più grande database di ricerca al mondo e potrebbe potenzialmente utilizzare i dati raccolti dagli utenti per completare automaticamente gli indirizzi email e altro ancora.
